entries.title: The Ghostlands
body: Once the southern part of Eversong, divided from the north only by the Elrendar River. It was home to Tranquillien, the largest town of the south, and to the Windrunner family. The Amani trolls of Zul'Aman have always kept their strength in these hills.

In the Third War the Scourge tore through these woods, razing towns and villages; human necromancers raised the fallen elves. The Farstriders under Sylvanas Windrunner fought a vicious but hopeless battle and were driven north. When it was over, the survivors named the blighted south the Ghostlands, for the dead now outnumbered the living. Since then, the magic that holds the rest of Quel'Thalas in eternal spring has passed it by.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Ghostlands (introduction, History, Third War and reclamation)

entries.title: Tranquillien
body: A blood elf town on the western slope of Sungraze Peak, overlooking the Dead Scar. The elves abandoned it as the Scourge advanced on the Sunwell, and have taken it back.

It is held by sin'dorei and Forsaken together, a partnership the elves accepted only reluctantly. Sylvanas offered troops and supplies many times before Quel'Thalas trusted her enough to let them in. Dame Auriferous and High Executor Mavren share command. The Scourge of Deatholme attacks the town often, supplies are always short and word from Silvermoon rarely comes.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Tranquillien (Third War, The Burning Crusade)

entries.title: Suncrown Village
body: Every year the elves of Suncrown held a ritual to keep the forces of nature under their control. Their mastery of water was shown by summoning and enslaving an elemental, Aquantion. One year Aquantion turned their own spellcasting against them, killed them all, and bound their spirits beneath Lake Elrendar.
The village was destroyed in the Scourge invasion, and nerubians of the Scourge under Anok'suten have nested in its ruins.

entries.title: Goldenmist Village
body: A high elf village in the north-west, where the Salonar sisters lived and Sylvanas Windrunner had friends. Its people were slain when the Scourge came, and they haunt its ruins still as ghosts and wraiths, the kind of tactic the Scourge favours.

entries.title: Windrunner Village
body: A village beneath Windrunner Spire, named for the family that protected it for centuries. The Scourge passed this way to Silvermoon, and Sylvanas fought it on the village's outskirts.

Gargoyles and the shades of the slain elves have haunted it ever since. When Quel'Thalas joined the Horde, the other leaders went to Silvermoon, but Sylvanas came here instead, alone, and remembered all the dead.

entries.title: Windrunner Spire
body: The home of the Windrunners on the western coast, where Alleria, Sylvanas and Vereesa grew up. Banshees of the Scourge and cultists from Deatholme have overrun it, and High Executor Mavren wants it taken back in the name of the Banshee Queen.

entries.title: Lake Elrendar
body: The lake on the border with Eversong was once bright; since the Scourge came it has turned murky and sick, and a damp mist blows off it. The drowned spirits of Suncrown Village haunt its waters.
Crypt fiends hold the Isle of Tribulations, north-east of Suncrown. Young Blood Knights come there for the first trial of their powers, to light a brazier in the cave on the isle.

entries.title: Farstrider Enclave
body: A Farstrider base on the southern shore of Lake Elrendar, cut off from the rest of the elves by ghosts on the lake, Shadowpine trolls to the east and south and lynxes on the land.

Halduron Brightwing and his rangers were here when they saw something strange at Dawnstar Spire and rode to the Regent Lord's aid. Afterwards it was here that Lor'themar and Halduron met Thrall, Cairne, Vol'jin and Sylvanas to bring Quel'Thalas into the Horde.

entries.title: Zeb'Sora
body: A small Shadowpine troll village on the east shore of Lake Elrendar. Lieutenant Tomathren of the Farstriders led a badly planned attack on it that cost many rangers their lives. He blames Ranger Valanna, and insists it would have worked if the rangers had only done as he told them.

entries.title: Zeb'Tela and Zeb'Nowa
body: Forest troll villages of the Amani in the eastern Ghostlands, near the Amani Pass that leads to Zul'Aman. Zeb'Nowa is the largest, sprawling across the south-east. With the elves weakened, the trolls press against the borders of Quel'Thalas once more.

entries.title: The Amani Catacombs
body: Forest troll crypts in the mountains north-east of Tranquillien. There are rumours that the mummified trolls inside are rising from the dead.

entries.title: Sanctum of the Sun
body: An arcane sanctum south-east of Tranquillien, still in working order, its turning orbs representing the stars. Its magisters lead the effort to free the Ghostlands from the Scourge and other invaders. A secret passage behind it leads through the mountains to Tranquillien.

entries.title: Sanctum of the Moon
body: An arcane sanctum just west of Tranquillien, once a testament to elven mastery of the arcane. It is partly destroyed now and overrun by arcane elementals and mana wyrms.

entries.title: Dawnstar Spire
body: The home of Dar'Khan Drathir before he turned to the Scourge. He grew up here, and later used it for his research, and his arcane reavers still guard it, on the eastern shore of Lake Elrendar.
It was here that Dar'Khan lured Lady Liadrin's new Blood Knights into a trap, and here that Lor'themar Theron arrived and killed him, for a time.

entries.title: The Ley-Line Nexuses
body: Three hidden places where the ley lines of Quel'Thalas fork. Each held a mooncrystal linked to Quel'Danas, and together they powered Ban'dinoriel, the great shield of Silvermoon; they were also the pieces of the Key of the Three Moons that could unlock its moongate. They were hidden by magic and guarded so that no invader would learn of them.

Dar'Khan told Arthas their secret. The Scourge slew the guardians and took the crystals; at An'owyn the death knight Thassarian led the attack, and only the ranger Koltira survived. At An'daroth, Lor'themar Theron lost his left eye fighting the risen elves, and was saved only by Halduron Brightwing's arrival. Now night elf Sentinels use the old crystal orbs to spy on Quel'Thalas.

entries.title: Shalandis Isle
body: The base of a night elf expedition of Sentinels on the western coast, their ship anchored offshore. From here they took over the old ley-line nexuses to watch the blood elves.

entries.title: Underlight Mines
body: A cluster of mines west of the Bleeding Ziggurat, home of a rare ore called underlight. The Blackpaw gnolls have overrun them, and the blood elves think the ore may prove useful against the Scourge.

entries.title: The Dead Scar
body: The path of destruction the Scourge left on its march to the Sunwell begins here at Deatholme and runs north through the Ghostlands, across the Elrendar and into Eversong. Undead still walk it.

entries.title: The Twin Ziggurats
body: Two identical Scourge ziggurats on either side of the Dead Scar. In each, three darkmages of the Deatholme cult guard an ancient artifact filled with the power of the Sunwell: the Stone of Flame in the Bleeding Ziggurat, the Stone of Light in the Howling Ziggurat. The Stone of Flame was imbued by Grand Magister Belo'vir Salonar.

entries.title: Deatholme
body: The Scourge citadel in the south-west where the Dead Scar begins, built on the withered roots of Thas'alah, the mother tree of Eversong, which the Scourge cut down. Arthas named it and gave it to the risen Dar'Khan. Ziggurats and slaughterhouses surround it.
It was here that Sylvanas, once free of the Lich King, came with her dark rangers and found her own body. Blood Knight Dawnstar died leading a failed assault on it.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Deatholme (Third War, The Burning Crusade)

entries.title: Tower of the Damned
body: The headquarters of Dar'Khan Drathir in the heart of Deatholme. The Eyes of Dar'Khan watch every entrance, necromancers and their skeletons fill the halls, and Dar'Khan himself waits at the centre with his lieutenants Mirdoran the Fallen, Borgoth the Bloodletter, Jurion the Deceiver and Masophet the Black.

entries.title: Thalassian Pass
body: The pass south through the mountains to the Plaguelands. Its great gatehouse is thought to be one of the Elfgates that sealed Quel'Thalas off from Lordaeron, the gates Dar'Khan opened for the Scourge. Scourge banners still hang beside them; the elves have been too disheartened by the fall to tear them down.

entries.title: Hatchet Hills and the Amani Pass
body: The hills leading to the Amani Pass, the road into Zul'Aman, capital of the forest trolls. Zul'Aman was built on the spot where the trolls slew one of the Old Gods' generals in ancient times, and in the Troll Wars the Amani Empire was the greatest power in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Silvermoon was raised over Amani burial grounds, an insult the trolls never forgot. In the Second War their warlord Zul'jin joined the Horde; captured and tortured by the Farstriders, he escaped and returned to Zul'Aman to recover. He rules there still.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Zul'Aman (Founding, Empire's Fall, Second War)

entries.title: Dar'Khan Drathir
body: Once an esteemed magister, Dar'Khan grew up at Dawnstar Spire and studied in Dalaran with Rommath and Umbric. A talented mage, he was arrogant and vindictive, and always felt denied the recognition he deserved. His bitterness made him an easy tool for the Lich King, and he opened the way for the Scourge into Quel'Thalas.

He has died many times, executed by Arthas, burned by the blue dragon Tyrygosa, destroyed by Anveena, and struck down by Lor'themar Theron's enchanted arrow, and every time he has come back. He rules the Scourge of Quel'Thalas from Deatholme, and while he lives on Silvermoon's doorstep, the blood elves cannot be fully accepted into the Horde.

entries.title: High Executor Mavren
body: The Forsaken commander Sylvanas sent to Tranquillien to help Dame Auriferous against Dar'Khan and the Scourge. Among his concerns is the Windrunner home, which he means to reclaim in the name of his queen.

entries.title: Dame Auriferous
body: The blood elf commander of Tranquillien, who shares the town with the Forsaken and holds it against Deatholme with little help from Silvermoon. The Farstriders are stretched too thin to reinforce her.

entries.title: Magister Kaendris
body: The magister in charge of the Sanctum of the Sun, who sends the boldest volunteers into the heart of the enemy: Dar'Khan's Tower of the Damned in Deatholme.

entries.title: Captain Helios
body: The commander of the Farstrider Enclave, whose rangers struggle against the relentless raids of the Amani trolls.

entries.title: The Fall of Quel'Thalas
body: The Scourge broke through the Elfgates with Dar'Khan's help, took the mooncrystals and killed their guardians, and swept north through the southern forest. Sylvanas and her Farstriders fought them village by village and were pushed back to Silvermoon, where she fell and Arthas raised her as a banshee.

When the elves recovered, they were divided. Some were content to stay in the north; others, like Lady Liadrin, would not rest until all Quel'Thalas was free. The new Blood Knights fought many of their first battles here, and it was in the Ghostlands that Dar'Khan ambushed them, set Lor'themar ablaze, and was struck down by the Regent Lord.

entries.title: Sin'dorei and Forsaken
body: The blood elves did not trust the Forsaken. Sylvanas offered supplies and soldiers again and again, and they refused, fearing a trick, before at last letting her people onto their land. Now the Forsaken stand with them at Tranquillien, and with their help the elves are making real progress against the Scourge. Quel'Thalas is still negotiating to join the Horde.

entries.title: Khadgar's Storm
body: In the Second War, the Old Horde set fire to Eversong, and the southern forest burned. Khadgar of the Kirin Tor called down a vast storm across the whole battlefront, exhausting all his magic. It made the fighting soggy and miserable, and put out the fires for a time, but the breath of the Horde's red dragons was so hot that trees soaked minutes before blackened and crumbled to ash in an instant.
